newsitem.title: USA: Brady bonds up, Argentina mega debt deal rumored.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds up, Argentina mega debt deal rumored.

text.p: Emerging debt prices were mostly higher in light pre-holiday trade as rumors of an Argentina global debt offering hit the market, traders said.
"The market is a little bit stronger today prices are up about 1/4 to 3/8 of a point on most of the major Latin credits boosted by a stronger U.S. Treasury market," said one emerging debt trader.
Meanwhile, rumors filled the market of an upcoming Argentina global issue of between $2.0 and $3.0 billion expected to be launched in January, traders said.

"There has been talk in the market of Argentina trying to bring some type of $2.0 to $3.0 billion debt offering," said one syndicate source. Another source cited "rumors of a pending deal for Argentina via underwriters JP Morgan and Merrill Lynch."
Although no official details have been made regarding the rumored deal, on Monday, economy minister Roque Fernandez said that Argentina was "studying the possibility" of a global bond issue in 1997.

Among other Brady issues, Bulgaria debt slid 1-1/2 points early Monday, triggered by a political crisis in the country, traders said. Congress delegates were preparing to vote in Sofia for a new premier and party leader following Saturday's surprise resignation of Bulgaria's prime minister, Zhav Videnov.
Traders said Bulgaria debt was quoted down 3/4 of a point late Monday after coming off its earlier lows.
At 1635 EST/2135 GMT, Bulgaria's IABs BGFLTH11=RR were off 7/8 at 51-1/4 bid and Bulgaria FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were off 3/8 at 38-3/8 bid, traders said.

Peru's when-issued Brady bonds recouped some of the steep losses suffered last week on the hostage situation in Lima following the Peruvian rebels release of 225 hostages late Sunday, traders said. Still, more than 140 people remained captive at the Japanese ambassador's home.
Peru debt was quoted up 1/4 to 3/8 in thin volume in New York trading, but emerging market debt sources said prices remained lower on the week.
In the broader market, Argentine pars AR4C23=RR were up 1/4 at 63-1/8 bid, Venezuelan Pars VZ675C20=RR were up 1/2 at 75-7/8 bid and Mexico Pars MX625L19=RR were up 1/8 at 73-1/8 bid.
Russia's dollar Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR continued stronger and was quoted up 1-1/8 at 78-5/8 bid.
Looking ahead, volume is expected to remain light as activity winds down for the Christmas Day holiday.
"There's going to be very light volume this week...the market will probably be given its general tone and direction from the U.S. Treasury market," said one trader.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was up 9/32 at 98-29/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
